A.explanation: Person at X is behind the vehicle moving away from X, so frequency cannot be higher than $750\text{ Hz}$.

B.explanation: Person at X hears a receding source so frequency is lower than $750\text{ Hz}$, not higher.

C.explanation: Person at X hears lower than $750\text{ Hz}$ decreasing further, and person at Y hears higher than $750\text{ Hz}$ increasing further as approach speed grows.

D.explanation: Person at Y hears an approaching source so frequency rises with speed, it does not decrease in frequency while accelerating toward Y.

hints: Notice from the direction of travel arrow that the vehicle moves away from X and toward Y, with source frequency $750\text{ Hz}$.
Connect approaching to compressed observed wavelength and higher observed frequency, and receding to stretched wavelength and lower observed frequency.
Think how increasing source speed during acceleration makes the Doppler shift larger for both the receding observer at X and the approaching observer at Y.
walkthrough: Identify the motion: the vehicle starts between X and Y and accelerates toward Y, so it recedes from the person at X and approaches the person at Y.
State the Doppler rule: for sound, an approaching source gives observed frequency $f_o > f_s$ and a receding source gives $f_o < f_s$, where $f_s = 750\text{ Hz}$.
Apply to X: the source moves away, observed wavelength is stretched, so the person at X hears lower than $750\text{ Hz}$.
Apply to Y: the source moves toward, observed wavelength is compressed, so the person at Y hears higher than $750\text{ Hz}$.
Add acceleration: larger source speed means a larger shift, so the low frequency at X drops further and the high frequency at Y rises further.
Match to the table: lower than $750\text{ Hz}$, decreasing in frequency at X and higher than $750\text{ Hz}$, increasing in frequency at Y. This is option C.
